# A mutation that stops the template type checking is not run.
#
# Emptying {{.Inner}} would leave {{$inner := ""}}, and {{$inner.Name}}
# below it would then read a field off a string. The tests would fail, but
# on a render error rather than on anything they assert, so counting that
# as a caught mutation would overstate the coverage.
#
# The type of dot is what makes this knowable before running anything,
# which is why mutants are checked against the ExecuteTemplate call that
# renders them.

muxt test-template-mutations --dry-run --seed 1
cmp stdout want.txt

-- go.mod --
module server

go 1.24
-- templates.gohtml --
{{define "page"}}{{$inner := .Inner}}{{$inner.Name}}{{end}}
-- template.go --
package server

import (
	"embed"
	"html/template"
	"io"
)

//go:embed *.gohtml
var templateFiles embed.FS

var templates = template.Must(template.ParseFS(templateFiles, "*.gohtml"))

type Inner struct {
	Name string
}

type Page struct {
	Inner Inner
}

func Render(w io.Writer, page Page) error {
	return templates.ExecuteTemplate(w, "page", page)
}
-- render_test.go --
package server

import (
	"strings"
	"testing"
)

func TestPage(t *testing.T) {
	var buf strings.Builder
	if err := Render(&buf, Page{Inner: Inner{Name: "hi"}}); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if got, want := buf.String(), "hi"; got != want {
		t.Errorf("page = %q, want %q", got, want)
	}
}
-- want.txt --
